Designing with code lets you see how an experience feels and behaves, from micro interactions to complete flows. But when everyone is working separately in their own coding tools, it can feel like you’re designing in isolation, making it harder to share work or compare alternatives.

That’s why [we introduced code layers earlier this year](https://www.figma.com/blog/code-on-the-figma-canvas/)

, bringing code onto the shared Figma canvas. Previously, exploring in code meant working in an IDE, which is disconnected from how many Figma users want to work. Code layers allows teams to build visually in code, with all the collaborative tools the Figma canvas provides. Teammates can try prototypes side by side, leave feedback alongside them, or duplicate a code layer to explore their own ideas, all in one place. Whether you’re converting existing designs into working code, bringing in a coded prototype from a third-party tool, local folder, or GitHub, or capturing what’s live on your website with the [Chrome extension](https://www.figma.com/downloads/chrome-extension/), code layers lets you keep building on the canvas.

## [Build from your existing work](#build-from-your-existing-work)

When you’re exploring a new product idea, sometimes it’s helpful to start from scratch. Other times, like when you're thinking of a new feature or flow, it's more efficient to start from your existing codebase. Code layers gives you several ways to build on existing work. Import a supported, lightweight prototyping codebase from GitHub or a local folder to build on the screens and interactions you already have. When you import from GitHub, the code layer stays connected to that repository.

![Prompting with agent in code layers](data:image/png;base64,)![Prompting with agent in code layers](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/e2a2ce577dc820b43d688545d2343d69cab12bff-3840x2160.png?rect=0,1,3840,2159&w=804&h=452&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)

Import your prototyping codebase from GitHub or a local folder to iterate on existing flows.

![Code on the canvas](data:image/png;base64,)![Code on the canvas](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/f2d5828083c2cd8625f94bae8fb2e4fbb80f49f1-3840x2160.png?rect=0,1,3840,2159&w=804&h=452&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)

Keep exploring your live web experience on the canvas with the Figma Chrome extension.

When Figma designer Maria Gaston wanted to make a prototype she’d built in an IDE easier to review with her team, she imported the code into a code layer using the Figma MCP server. “Working in the coding tool made it hard to share work and iterate,” she says. “It was a very isolated environment. Now, everyone else who has access to this file can easily go in and play with it.”

The [Figma Chrome extension](https://www.figma.com/downloads/chrome-extension/) gives you the power to bring your live web experience onto the canvas as a code layer, so you can keep exploring changes alongside the original page.

For example, at Cox Automotive, which provides software and services for car dealerships, senior product manager Lindsay Brechler brought an existing HTML prototype into code layers to align stakeholders on a new feature. Because every version stayed on the canvas, Lindsay could pick up from any one of them and keep iterating without starting from scratch. “From iteration to iteration, code layers holds every screen and interaction together very well,” Lindsay says.

You can also turn a Figma design into an interactive code layer. At Rocket Money, Derek Onay, Lead Product Designer for Design Systems, uses this method to share early ideas with his team. When the team was building foundational screen components, it was important to settle interactions and accessibility early, before they affected people using the product. Derek built a concept in a code layer to drive those conversations. “With code layers, the real value is in having the ability to better communicate ideas and gain stakeholder alignment,” he says. “I can share a working prototype and meet my team where they already are, in Figma.”

Beyond existing code and designs, you can bring a prototype from your coding tool onto the canvas through [Figma’s MCP server](https://www.figma.com/blog/the-tldr-on-mcp/)

, or capture your live web page as a code layer with the [Figma Chrome extension](https://www.figma.com/downloads/chrome-extension/).

## [Explore and build together](#explore-and-build-together)

###### Customer snapshot: Merkle

Merkle, a global customer experience agency, uses code layers across its entire design and build process, from blank-canvas ideation to iterating on existing features already built in code. The impact:

→ 30% faster iteration and feature development.

→ 50% less documentation, such as interaction specs on tickets.

When you’re working with coding agents in an IDE, it’s easy to latch onto your first idea before you’ve considered the alternatives. With code layers, multiple versions of a prototype can sit on the canvas at the same time: You and your team can duplicate a prototype, try a different approach, and compare both versions without switching between them.

Miguel Wermuth, a product designer at Dell Technologies, works on the customer account experience for both enterprise customers and dell.com shoppers across mobile, tablet, and desktop. He uses code layers to bring conversational AI experiences, where a stakeholder can type a question and the prototype responds with the right screen, onto the canvas. Once a flow is approved by fellow designers, Miguel builds it out in code layers to get sign-off from business stakeholders, who find a working prototype easier to follow than a series of static screens. To compare versions, he duplicates code layers side by side on the canvas. “With code layers, I can work with code while designing on the canvas. It’s really powerful to have more back and forth between design and code.”

###### Code layers tip

Mirror a code layer in the Figma mobile app to review it on the go.

But it's not just about evaluating one direction; code layers allows you to zoom out and look at a product experience holistically. As Matt Davey, Chief Experience Officer at 1Password, puts it: “The real superpower of Figma has always been the canvas. It’s like when we used to print out all the pages of a website and stick them on a whiteboard. Being able to look at these UI elements together is incredibly valuable.”

> The real superpower of Figma has always been the canvas. Being able to look at these UI elements together is incredibly valuable.

Matt Davey, Chief Experience Officer, 1Password

## [Refine without leaving code behind](#refine-without-leaving-code-behind)

###### Customer snapshot: Superside

You can also refine a code layer’s interactions by prompting the Figma agent. At Superside, motion design lead Leonardo Rica used prompts to develop a credit card wallet code layer where users can scroll through cards, tap one to bring it forward, and flip it over. When cards were briefly stacking in the wrong order, Leonardo described the cause in a single, precise prompt, and the Figma agent fixed it “like magic.”

As you refine an idea, code layers lets you make design adjustments and apply them to the working prototype. For visual changes you’d rather make directly, `Extract designs` turns a screen or flow from a code layer into editable Figma layers.

At Checkout.com, Senior Product Designer Kris Murphy, works on products that businesses integrate into their own customer experiences. When a prospective client wanted to see the technology in action, Kris built a demo in code layers. “Code layers helped me build the demo about 50% faster, and that’s with a tool I’m not entirely familiar with yet,” Kris says. Before sharing the demo with a client, Kris wanted to make sure every screen was polished. Instead of clicking through the prototype screen by screen, he pulled every screen out of the code layer onto the Figma canvas. From there, it was easy to review them side by side to catch and fix anything that needed to be reworked. Kris then sent those edits back to the code layer, and the Checkout.com team could review the full flow of revisions made on the canvas, too. “Code layers feels like a proper bridge between design and development,” he says. “It’s helped me ideate and deliver at speed.”

![Map with numbered clusters of items for sale beside an AI prompt: “Add a cluster feature to all items for sale on our map.”](data:image/png;base64,)![Map with numbered clusters of items for sale beside an AI prompt: “Add a cluster feature to all items for sale on our map.”](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/e4f9b327e9bb0559859cbb355b63323d10e4cd64-1920x1080.png?rect=0,1,1920,1079&w=804&h=452&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)

Ask the Figma agent to add functionality, like interactive map features, to a code layer.

###### Code layers tip

You can also merge ideas from different versions of the prototype. If the team likes the layout of one and the interactions in another, they can ask the Figma agent to combine them into a new version to test.

Other editing options include commenting directly on a prototype, annotating a prototype’s frames to show the agent where a change is needed, or inspecting and editing the code directly. And the newly updated fullscreen experience allows you to work with multiple threads with the agent for different parts of the work.

Once you’re ready to share your changes, you can push the updated code to a branch so teammates can continue to build off the prototype. Creating a pull request lets your team review those changes before merging them into the shared project.

![Extract designs](data:image/png;base64,)![Extract designs](https://cdn.sanity.io/images/599r6htc/regionalized/186f422e55b6e4d04f695a00f06e799e333f63b1-3840x2160.png?rect=0,1,3840,2159&w=804&h=452&q=75&fit=max&auto=format)

Use \`Extract designs\` to turn screens from a code layer into editable Figma frames.

Code layers is [rolling out in open beta](https://help.figma.com/hc/en-us/articles/44193259600535-Code-layers-in-Figma-Design) starting today, and will use AI credits. On paid plans, creating and editing within code layers is free through November 4, 2026.
